task_description: A multi-hop web lookup on Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute (LII). The solver must: (1) take the fifth federal-rules section alphabetically (Appellate, Bankruptcy, Civil, Criminal, Evidence -> Federal Rules of Evidence); (2) find the article within it having 'witnesses' in the most titles as of 2021 (Article VI. Witnesses); (3) take that article's first rule (Rule 601); (4) read the LII committee notes for the last amendment and report the single word that was deleted. The gold answer is 'inference' -- the word removed in the 2011 restyling redline of Rule 601's committee text.
final_vs_expected: produced None (no FINAL ANSWER ever emitted; team's working answer was 'except') vs gold 'inference' -- the team both failed to finalize AND its working answer was the wrong deleted word
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: after the substantive answer was posted at Turn 1, the selector re-routed to WebResearcher for ~20 turns (and never to a Finalizer), so no FINAL ANSWER was emitted and the run hit the message cap.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): no agent ever emits 'FINAL ANSWER'; despite a correct-looking working answer by Turn 7, the chat loops to the cap with no finalize action and Finalizer is never selected. 1.3 (Step repetition): WebResearcher republishes 'except' (or empty) verbatim across Turns 8-29 with no new work -- e.g. Turns 14,15,19,21,22,23,24,25,26,28,29 all just say 'except'. 3.2 (No/incomplete verification): the Critic (Turns 2,6) repeatedly names exactly what is missing -- evidence for 'fifth section alphabetically' and 'most titles with witnesses as of 2021' -- but no agent ever runs the count/ranking or re-reads the committee-note redline; verification is requested but never performed. 3.1 (Premature-style termination by cap): the run terminates (cap) before the task is actually solved and before any answer is finalized.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector picks WebResearcher, which runs a 7-round ReAct loop. It correctly fetches /federal and /rules/fre, correctly identifies Federal Rules of Evidence as the fifth alphabetical section and Article VI. Witnesses / Rule 601, then fetches the Rule 601 page. But it only compares the CURRENT rule text ('unless these rules provide otherwise') to the pre-2011 wording quoted in an advisory note ('except as otherwise provided in these rules') and concludes the deleted word is 'except' -- it never reads the 2011 restyling redline where 'inference' was deleted. It publishes 'except'. Turn 2: Critic correctly accepts the article/rule mapping as plausible but flags that the clue-selection (fifth-section, most-witnesses-titles count) is unverified and asks WebResearcher for exact posted page evidence and Analyst for the count. Turn 3: WebResearcher republishes the same 'except' conclusion with URLs but does NOT supply the count/ranking the Critic asked for. Turns 4-5: Analyst is selected twice but does no run_python computation -- it just restates 'except' from the posted text. Turn 6: Critic again says the word is supported but the full clue match remains unverified. Turns 7-29: the run collapses -- the selector picks WebResearcher almost every turn (and Analyst once, Turn 15), and the chosen agent either repeats 'except', acknowledges the gap, or publishes an empty message. No agent ever performs the missing count, re-checks the redline, or emits a FINAL ANSWER. Finalizer is never selected. The run hits the message cap with no answer.
open_ended_diagnosis: Two distinct faults compound. (A) A single-agent capability/verification miss at Turn 1: WebResearcher diffed the rule's BODY text instead of the committee-note redline, so it landed on 'except' rather than the gold 'inference'. The LII page does contain the redline, but the agent stopped searching once it had a plausible diff. (B) The dominant fault, and the reason outcome=no_answer rather than wrong_answer, is structural non-convergence in the selector + a missing termination pathway. After Turn ~7 there is nothing left for the team to do that any agent will actually execute: the Critic keeps naming the unmet 'count/ranking' requirement, but neither WebResearcher nor Analyst ever does that work (Analyst never even calls run_python), and crucially the selector NEVER routes to Finalizer, so the one action that could end the run is structurally unreachable. The selector's own reasoning shows it stuck in a deliberation loop -- e.g. Turn 21: 'There might be a counting clue related to most titles as of 2021, so the Analyst might need to count titles? However, I'll need web access for that... The WebResearcher could help verify' -- repeatedly re-deriving 'route to WebResearcher' without ever advancing or finalizing. The agents devolve into echoing a single token ('except') or empty strings, a degenerate fixed point. This is a harness/topology failure (no forced finalize, selector with no progress pressure), not genuine inter-agent deception or distortion.
reasoning_vs_published: Turn 1 reasoning-vs-published is faithful but wrong: the WebResearcher privately reasons 'except was removed during a 2011 restyling... I'll confirm that except was indeed the deleted word' and publishes exactly that -- no distortion, the private conclusion was simply incorrect (it never inspected the redline that deleted 'inference'). The Critic's published input IS substantive and correct ('There is no posted evidence supporting ... most titles ... no count or comparison was shown'), but it is effectively IGNORED: Turn 4 Analyst's private reasoning even acknowledges the gap -- 'I should clarify that the word except is deleted but point out that the clue isn't fully verified' -- yet it publishes only 'except' with no computation, satisfying the FORM of responding to the Critic without its SUBSTANCE (false-trust / verification theater, the count is never run). From Turn 8 onward most rounds emit '(no reasoning summary emitted)' and publish either 'except' or '(empty)', showing the agents had no new private thinking to convey -- the divergence is not info-distortion but content exhaustion. The selector's reasoning is the clearest signal of the actual failure: across Turns 9,16,19,21,24,26,27 it repeatedly muses that an Analyst might be needed for counting but 'we need a Web Researcher first', never concluding to finalize and never picking Finalizer -- a selector-misrouting loop, quoted at Turn 24: 'The WebResearcher didn't address the missing clue logic and just repeated support. Since the question appears to need a finalizer, this situation feels a bit tricky' -- it recognizes a finalizer is needed yet still selects WebResearcher.
